text: By the time the repaired sluice gates at Tamsin Reservoir began turning again last week, the basin had already spent three winters under temporary restrictions. The 48 million repair bill, confirmed by the Northfold Water Board in its annual accounts, covered reinforcement of the eastern embankment, replacement of two cracked spillway channels and a full overhaul of the 1978 control house. The reservoir, built on the edge of Bracken Moor in 1964, has long been a quiet fixture of the valley, supplying water to seven settlements and a scattering of farms. Engineers began the works in March 2023 after seepage was detected near the southern bank. Residents welcomed the reopening, though many noted that the cost reflected years of deferred maintenance.
